questions.question: A plano-convex lens of focal length $f$ is split into two identical plano-convex lenses. One half is placed on top of the other, such that their convex surfaces are in contact, forming a bi-convex lens. The equivalent focal length of this combination will be

options.explanation: Incorrect calculation of equivalent focal length
Correct calculation of equivalent focal length using the formula $ rac{1}{F_{eq}} =  rac{1}{f_1} +  rac{1}{f_2}$
Incorrect calculation of equivalent focal length
Incorrect calculation of equivalent focal length

questions.explanation: Let the original plano-convex lens have refractive index $n$ and radius of curvature $R$ for its curved surface. Its focal length $f$ is given by: $ rac{1}{f} = (n-1) \left(\frac{1}{R} - \frac{1}{\infty}\right) = \frac{n-1}{R}$ When the plano-convex lens is split, each half is still a plano-convex lens with the same radius of curvature $R$. So, each half has a focal length $f$. When two such plano-convex lenses are placed with their convex surfaces in contact, they form a combination of two thin lenses in contact. The equivalent focal length $F_{eq}$ of the combination is given by: $ rac{1}{F_{eq}} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2}$ Since each half has focal length $f$, we have $f_1 = f$ and $f_2 = f$. $ rac{1}{F_{eq}} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{f} = \frac{2}{f}$ $F_{eq} = \frac{f}{2}$

questions.explanation: For Lens L1: Object distance $u_1 = -30 \text{ cm}$ (left of L1) Focal length $f_1 = +10 \text{ cm}$ Using the lens formula: $ rac{1}{v_1} -  rac{1}{u_1} =  rac{1}{f_1}$ $ rac{1}{v_1} -  rac{1}{-30} =  rac{1}{10}$ $ rac{1}{v_1} +  rac{1}{30} =  rac{1}{10}$ $ rac{1}{v_1} =  rac{1}{10} -  rac{1}{30} =  rac{3-1}{30} =  rac{2}{30} =  rac{1}{15}$ $v_1 = +15 \text{ cm}$ The image I1 formed by L1 is real, $15 \text{ cm}$ to the right of L1. For Lens L2: Lens L2 is $40 \text{ cm}$ to the right of L1. The image I1 acts as the object for L2. Distance of I1 from L2 = (Distance between L1 and L2) - (Distance of I1 from L1) $d = 40 \text{ cm} - 15 \text{ cm} = 25 \text{ cm}$ Since I1 is to the left of L2, the object distance for L2 is $u_2 = -25 \text{ cm}$. Focal length $f_2 = +20 \text{ cm}$ Using the lens formula for L2: $ rac{1}{v_2} -  rac{1}{u_2} =  rac{1}{f_2}$ $ rac{1}{v_2} -  rac{1}{-25} =  rac{1}{20}$ $ rac{1}{v_2} +  rac{1}{25} =  rac{1}{20}$ $ rac{1}{v_2} =  rac{1}{20} -  rac{1}{25} =  rac{5-4}{100} =  rac{1}{100}$ $v_2 = +100 \text{ cm}$ The final image is real, $100 \text{ cm}$ to the right of L2.

questions.question: Two thin lenses of focal lengths $f_1$ and $f_2$ are placed in contact. What is the power of the combination, $P_{comb}$?

options.explanation: This is partially correct but does not explicitly show the relationship in terms of focal lengths.

All the given expressions are equivalent representations of the power of the lens combination.

questions.explanation: The power of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length ($P = 1/f$). When two thin lenses are placed in contact, their powers add up because the combined focal length $f_{comb}$ is given by $1/f_{comb} = 1/f_1 + 1/f_2$. Thus, $P_{comb} = P_1 + P_2 = 1/f_1 + 1/f_2 = (f_1 + f_2)/(f_1 f_2)$.
questions.hint: Recall that the power of a lens is $P = 1/f$ and that powers add for lenses in contact.

questions.explanation: For lenses in contact, the equivalent focal length $F$ is given by $\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2}$. For a convex lens, $f_1 = +20\text{ cm}$, and for a concave lens, $f_2 = -10\text{ cm}$. Substituting these values: $\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{-10} = \frac{1}{20} - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{-1}{20}$. Thus, $F = -20\text{ cm}$. A negative focal length indicates a concave lens.

options.explanation: The image is formed at infinity because the net power of the lens combination is 1/100 and the object is at a distance of 100 cm.

questions.explanation: The power of the convex lens is 1/20 and the power of the concave lens is -1/25. The net power is 1/20 - 1/25 = 1/100. Using the lens equation, 1/f = 1/v - 1/u, we get 1/100 = 1/v - 1/(-100). Solving for v, we get v = -100 * 100 / (100 - 100) which tends to infinity.
